q: Which statement accurately summarizes the findings about vision-related fall-prevention interventions described in Hazzard?
o: Vision interventions produced different fall outcomes across trials and patient groups
Vision assessment with treatment consistently reduced falls across the reported trials
Multifocal glasses improved recognition of hazards close to ground level
Home-safety modification increased falls among people with severe visual impairment
explanation:
Visual interventions change different parts of the task of walking safely. **The outcome depends on the intervention and the people receiving it.**

**A. Different outcomes across trials** — First-eye cataract surgery reduced falls. Routine correction had mixed results, while single-distance lenses plus counseling helped an outdoor-active subgroup.
**B. Consistent benefit of treating vision** — One trial showed no significant reduction and another recorded more falls following assessment and treatment.
**C. Multifocals improve ground-level vision** — The lower segment can blur a pavement edge when the wearer looks down.
**D. More falls after home modification** — Targeted home assessment and modification reduced falls among people with severe, uncorrectable visual impairment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 639–640.

q: For which stage of Alzheimer disease does Hazzard explicitly describe an approved indication for memantine?
o: Alzheimer disease with moderate-to-severe dementia
Early Alzheimer disease with mild dementia
Mild cognitive impairment before dementia develops
Subjective memory concerns without objective impairment
explanation:
Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist used for symptomatic treatment as Alzheimer dementia advances. The indication depends on clinical severity and daily impairment.

**Moderate-to-severe Alzheimer dementia** is the stage in which memantine is indicated.

**A. Moderate-to-severe dementia.** Modest benefits in cognition, function or behavior make this the appropriate disease stage.
**B. Mild dementia.** A diagnosis of early Alzheimer dementia alone does not supply the established memantine indication.
**C. Mild cognitive impairment.** Independence is preserved, and memantine has no established role in preventing conversion to dementia.
**D. Subjective memory concern.** First determine whether objective decline or functional impairment exists.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 911.

pamidronate (aredia)
Calcium supplement with vitamin D

explanation:
Myeloma-associated osteolysis predisposes to additional fractures even when serum calcium is normal. **Intravenous pamidronate reduces skeletal events in active myeloma with lytic lesions.**

**A. Denosumab (Prolia)** — Denosumab also has a myeloma indication as the oncology formulation Xgeva, given at a different dose and interval. Prolia is the osteoporosis regimen named here.
**B. Pamidronate** — This intravenous bisphosphonate inhibits bone resorption and is appropriate for preventing further skeletal complications. Assess renal function before administration.
**C. Calcium and vitamin D** — Supplementation may support bone health when appropriate, but cannot replace a bone-modifying agent for myeloma-related lytic disease.
**D. Calcitonin** — Its short-term calcium-lowering role does not provide durable prevention of myeloma fractures. The patient's calcium is normal.

q: מה מאפיין את השינויים במערכת השתן בגיל המבוגר?
o: רוב הקשישים עם אי שליטה על שתן סובלים מהתכווצויות לא רצוניות של השלפוחית (involuntary bladder contractions)
שאריות שתן לאחר ריקון ( residual urine volume) יורדת עם הגיל
קיבולת השלפוחית (functional bladder capacity ) עולה עם הגיל
בנשים בנות 80 ומעלה יש עליה בסיכון לאי שליטה על שתן ככל שעברו יותר לידות
explanation:
Aging can bring involuntary detrusor contractions as well as reduced functional capacity and incomplete emptying. **Involuntary contractions are common in older incontinent patients and may coexist with impaired mobility.**

**A. Most older incontinent patients have involuntary contractions** — The reported prevalence is 40% to 75% in older incontinent patients, so a majority occurs in some series. Such contractions can also occur without leakage.
**B. Residual volume decreases** — Residual volume generally increases with age.
**C. Functional capacity increases** — Functional capacity tends to decrease.
**D. Risk rises with increasing parity after age 80** — The association with previous childbirth becomes weaker beyond age 65. Parity is a less discriminating explanation in the oldest women.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, p. 701.

Key note: The accepted choice says “most.” The reported range of 40% to 75% includes cohorts below and above half. The childbirth association weakens after age 65, and the chapter gives no parity-specific threshold for women over 80.

q: על פי המאמר Time to Clinical Benefit of Intensive Blood Pressure Lowering in Patients 60 Years and Older With Hypertension מאת Chen וחבריו ב- JAMA 2022 מה ההשפעה של איזון אגרסיבי של לחץ הדם על MACE- Major adverse cardiovascular events?
o: לא הוכחה יעילות של איזון אגרסיבי של לחץ הדם במניעת MACE באנשים בני 60 ומעלה
האיזון האגרסיבי מונע אירוע אחד של MACE ל- 100 אנשים בשלוש שנים
איזון אגרסיבי של לחץ הדם מומלץ רק באנשים שתוחלת חייהם המשוערת היא יותר מ- 5 שנים
איזון אגרסיבי של לחץ הדם הוכח רק במטופלים עם סוכרת
explanation:
Time to benefit is the time needed for treatment to prevent a defined number of events. In six blood-pressure target trials enrolling adults aged 60 or older, **intensive treatment prevented one major cardiovascular event per 100 people treated for about three years**.

**A. No demonstrated benefit after age 60** — Major cardiovascular events were less frequent with intensive treatment. The pooled hazard ratio was 0.79 (95% CI 0.71–0.88).
**B. One event per 100 in three years** — A one-percentage-point absolute reduction took an estimated 34.4 months (95% CI 22.7–59.8). A smaller benefit of one event per 200 took 19.1 months.
**C. Only if life expectancy exceeds five years** — There was no fixed five-year cutoff. Weigh prognosis and the early risks of hypotension or kidney injury against the expected time to benefit.
**D. Benefit only in diabetes** — The trials included adults with and without diabetes. Diabetes was not a necessary condition for benefit.

Reference · Chen et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2022, pp. 660–667, doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2022.1657.

q: מה גורם ל-INTRINSIC ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY?
o: אי ספיקת לב אקוטית משנית ל- MALIGNANT HYPERTENSION
HYPOCALCEMIA
תת תזונה
HEMOLYTIC-UREMIC SYNDROME
explanation:
AKI can arise from reduced perfusion, injury within the kidney or urinary obstruction. **Hemolytic–uremic syndrome directly injures the renal microvasculature. Malignant hypertension can also damage renal vessels**, while acute heart failure caused by severe hypertension may reduce renal perfusion.

**A. Acute heart failure from malignant hypertension** — Heart failure may lower renal perfusion. Severe hypertension can also directly injure renal arterioles, which is a separate intrinsic mechanism.
**B. Hypocalcemia** — Low calcium is not classified as an intrinsic cause in this differential. Severe hypercalcemia is the calcium disorder listed.
**C. Malnutrition** — Low albumin can reduce effective circulating volume and contribute to prerenal injury.
**D. Hemolytic–uremic syndrome** — Thrombotic microangiopathy injures the kidney's small vessels, making this an intrinsic renal cause.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1281–1282, Table 83-1.
Key note: Table 83-1 places acute cardiac failure from malignant hypertension in the prerenal column and hemolytic–uremic syndrome in the intrinsic column. The examination accepts both.

צלוליטיס

explanation:
FAST 7c describes advanced loss of function including inability to walk independently. The hospice criteria also look for a recent qualifying complication, including intake insufficient to sustain life.

**Albumin of 2.2 g/dL falls below the 2.5 g/dL nutritional threshold.** This threshold illustrates inadequate nutrition in tube-fed patients and cannot independently predict six-month survival.

**A. Three stage 2 pressure ulcers.** Multiple ulcers qualify when they are stage 3 or 4. Increasing the number at stage 2 does not meet that criterion.
**B. Cellulitis.** Uncomplicated cellulitis is outside the specified infection criteria, which include septicemia and pyelonephritis.
**C. MMSE below 5.** A low cognitive score is no additional medical complication once functional stage has been specified.
**D. Albumin 2.2 g/dL.** It meets the numerical component of the nutrition criterion in the appropriate intake and feeding context.

q: בן 94 הסובל מדמנציה מתקדמת מאושפז עקב דלקת ריאות. הוא מקבל קו שלישי של טיפול אנטיביוטי ללא שיפור, פיתח אי ספיקה כלייתית והוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות במצב סופי. החולה מעורפל הכרה, לא אוכל ולא שותה. מה הטיפול המתאים לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות?
o: חייב לקבל מזון ונוזלים אפילו באמצעים מלאכותיים
חייב לקבל נוזלים אלא אם כן הרופא האחראי החליט שהנוזלים יכולים לגרום לנזק
הרופא האחראי צריך לשאול את המשפחה איזה טיפול החולה היה רוצה לקבל
אם אין הנחיות מקדימות או ייפוי כוח חייב לקבל עירוי נוזלים
explanation:
סעיף 17 מייחד את החולה בשלב סופי שאינו בעל כשרות, סובל סבל משמעותי ונקבע כדין שאינו רוצה בהארכת חייו. לעניין נוזלים נקבע סייג מיוחד גם במצב זה.
**יש לתת נוזלים, גם באמצעים מלאכותיים אם צריך, אלא אם הרופא האחראי קובע שמתן הנוזלים גורם לחולה סבל או נזק.**

**א. חובת מזון ונוזלים כאחד** סעיף 17 מבחין בין מזון לנוזלים כשהתנאים מתקיימים. אין להחיל על שניהם אותה חובה.
**ב. נוזלים והחריג שבאחריות הרופא** מבין האפשרויות זו מזהה את הכלל ואת בעל הסמכות. יש לבדוק את ההשפעה על החולה המסוים ולתעד את הקביעה.
**ג. לשאול את המשפחה** בירור רצונו של החולה עשוי לכלול את המשפחה. הוא אינו מחליף את ההוראה הספציפית בדבר מתן נוזלים.
**ד. עירוי בהיעדר מסמך** העדר הנחיה כתובה אינו מחייב דווקא עירוי ואינו מבטל את החריג בשל סבל או נזק.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 5, 8(ב), 16–17.
Key note: בסעיף 17 הניסוח הוא שמתן הנוזלים גורם סבל או נזק. אפשרות ב׳ מזכירה אפשרות לנזק בלבד, ואינה מציינת את הסבל או את יתר תנאי הסעיף.

q: A woman performs a cough stress test while standing with a comfortably full bladder. Which observation documents stress urinary incontinence?
o: Leakage begins several seconds after the cough has ended
The cough triggers the initiation of a sustained void
No leakage occurs while the bladder contains very little urine
Urine leakage occurs at the same time as the cough
explanation:
A cough stress test challenges outlet closure with a brief increase in abdominal pressure. **Leakage at the same moment as the cough documents stress incontinence.**

**A. Leakage begins several seconds after the cough has ended** — Delayed leakage may mean the cough provoked a detrusor contraction.
**B. The cough triggers the initiation of a sustained void** — A sustained void suggests detrusor activation rather than an isolated pressure leak.
**C. No leakage occurs while the bladder contains very little urine** — An underfilled bladder makes the test insensitive, so this observation cannot exclude stress leakage.
**D. Urine leakage occurs at the same time as the cough** — Simultaneous leakage links the pressure rise directly to failure of urethral closure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, p. 705.

explanation:
Profound hypotension, jugular venous distension and clear lungs during acute MI point toward right ventricular infarction. **Obtain right-sided ECG leads, especially V4R**, to detect acute right ventricular ST elevation.

**A. Liver ultrasound.** Right upper abdominal discomfort may reflect hepatic congestion but does not localize myocardial infarction.
**B. Serum potassium.** Useful for managing arrhythmias, but it does not confirm RV infarction.
**C. Right-sided ECG.** This is a rapid bedside extension of the standard tracing while stabilizing the patient.
**D. CT angiography.** Other vascular diagnoses may require CT, but right-sided leads address this immediate clinical suspicion more directly.
